Arboreal

/ar-BOR-ee-ul/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Arboreal means relating to trees, or living in and among them.

Arboreal means relating to trees, or living in and among them. Tree frogs are thoroughly arboreal, spending nearly their whole lives on leaves and branches high above the forest floor.

Worked Example

A three-toed sloth is born in the branches, feeds on the leaves within reach, sleeps hooked to a limb, and descends to the ground only once every week or so. Its curved claws grip bark easily but make walking on flat earth clumsy and slow. Even its fur grows in the direction that sheds rain while the animal hangs upside down. Every part of the sloth fits an arboreal life.

The sloth's body and daily routine are built for living in trees rather than on the ground, which is what arboreal describes.

How Arboreal Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

tree-dwelling

tree-dwelling: making its home in trees

sylvan

sylvan: belonging to the woods and trees

Antonyms

terrestrial

terrestrial: living on the ground

aquatic

aquatic: living in water

How Strong Is It? — wooded → arboreal → epiphytic

wooded vs. arboreal

wooded vs. arboreal: A wooded place merely has trees standing in it, while an arboreal creature actually lives up in them.

epiphytic vs. arboreal

epiphytic vs. arboreal: An arboreal animal lives among the branches, but an epiphytic plant goes further, growing directly on a tree's bark and never touching soil at all.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of arboreal.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — arbor

Root — arbor: from Latin arbor, tree

Suffix — eal

Suffix — eal: characteristic of, pertaining to (a spelling variant of -al)

Put it together

Put it together: Arboreal joins the Latin root arbor ('tree') to the suffix -al, spelled -eal here after the r, meaning 'characteristic of, pertaining to.' Put the pieces together and the word says 'characteristic of trees,' which is why an arboreal animal is one whose whole life belongs to the branches.

Use the root in a new word: arboretum

Use the root in a new word: arboretum: A city arboretum is a garden kept for the trees themselves, growing straight out of the Latin arbor that also gives us arboreal.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal, scientific (biology) register

Arboreal most often describes animals and their habits, as in 'arboreal snakes' or 'an arboreal lifestyle,' and it stands in contrast to terrestrial, meaning ground-dwelling. It can also describe anything of or about trees, as in 'the park's arboreal survey.'
